correctness.rationale: The trace identities give 32 T_B(k)=B_{2k+1}-(2k+1)=P_{2k}C_{k+1}-2k. In the binomial expansion at odd t=2k+1 the combined j=1,2 terms are 2t(t^2-1)(t^2+1)/15 and have valuation v2(t^2-1)+2; every higher term has the additional factor t^2-9 divisible by 8 after accounting for the factorial against 4^j. This gives the claimed valuation for every k, including k=1. The consecutive-window differences are P_{2k} P_{4n+2k}/4; strong divisibility (already on the first two indices) yields difference gcd P_{2k}/2 at odd k and 3P_{2k} at even k. Taking the gcd with T_B(k) gives the stated power of 2 using v2(P_j)=v2(j). For odd primes the numerator reduces to -2k modulo P_{2k}; at 3 in even windows, the normalized P_{4j}/12 has valuation v3(j), as seen from its mod-3 recurrence and the triplication multiplier 3 mod 9. Thus the extra factor 3 in the difference gcd cannot change the answer. The argument is all-index; the supplied finite test was inspected, not used as proof.

Hence v2(T_B(k))=v2(k+1)-1, extending the known prefix valuation mechanically to all k. The odd-index lemma is the same valuation via 32 T_B(k)=B_{2k+1}-(2k+1). The companion GCD likewise supplies no uncovered claim.
